summary: Sh. Ali Mashhour delivers a comprehensive lecture on the roles and contributions of women in Islam, with particular emphasis on the wives and female family members of the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) and other messengers. The lecture centers on Aisha (may Allah be pleased with her) and discusses how women played critical roles in supporting prophets and messengers in fulfilling their divine missions. Sh. Ali Mashhour references the beginning of revelation (wahy) with true dreams (ar-ru'ya as-saliha) and explains how the Prophet's wives, particularly Khadijah (may Allah be pleased with her), provided essential support during the initial revelation in the Cave of Hira. He emphasizes that these women's positions as mothers, sisters, and wives were not diminished roles but rather crucial positions that enabled the prophets to accomplish their ordained duties, countering modern Western attitudes that dismiss such roles.
suggested_title: The Essential Roles of Women in Islamic History: Mothers, Sisters, and Wives of the Prophets
